_readme: Each key below is a schema name. taxonomy.json assigns a schema to a
folder subtree using a '_schema' field, and a default author using a
'_default_author' field. Both cascade: every folder below inherits its
nearest ancestor's value unless it (or something closer) overrides it.
AUTHOR MODEL: most schemas below carry an optional per-item 'author'
field. Use it only when a single folder mixes works by different
authors (rare). Normally you don't need to set it per item - the
generator already writes the resolved '_default_author' into each
folder's data.json as 'default_author', so every item in that folder
is attributed correctly without repeating it. Set the item-level
'author' only to override that default for one specific item.
The generator does NOT copy these field lists into every data.json -
each data.json just stores {'schema', 'default_author', 'items': []}.
This file is the single source of truth for what belongs in 'items'.
'type' values are documentation hints (string / string[] / object[] /
number / boolean) - JSON itself doesn't enforce them.
CROSS-REFERENCE + SEARCH SPINE (added in the v2 reconciliation pass): every
schema below now carries two common optional item-level fields regardless
of its type-specific fields -- 'references' and 'tags' -- so cross-library
search and citation-linking work uniformly across every content type. Each
schema also declares 'primaryTextField' (a schema-level property, not an
item field) so the search-index generator knows which field holds the main
searchable text for that type without hardcoding per-schema logic -- null
means the text lives inside a nested array (e.g. itihasa_purana_text's
'shlokas'), which the generator flattens instead.

generic.description: Fallback schema for folders with no specific content model yet (Pancharatra Agama, Dharmashastra digests, Sutras, Ancillary Vedangas).

id.notes: short unique key within this folder

author.notes: override this folder's default_author, if different

references.notes: [{target, unit_id, note}] -- target is another grantha's slug (e.g. 'puranas/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10'), unit_id is that grantha's own item id being pointed at (e.g. '10.29.1'). Used to build the library-wide backlinks index (see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md) so 'what cites this verse' works without scanning the whole corpus.

tags.notes: free-form keywords for cross-library search -- independent of the taxonomy path itself.

vedic_text.description: Samhita mantras/riks, Brahmana/Aranyaka passages, and Upanishad sections. Used for every folder under 'vedas'. Fields are mostly optional because presence varies by layer (e.g. svara notation and devata mainly apply to Samhita mantras, not Brahmana prose; padapatha may not exist for every shakha). No 'author' field - Vedas are traditionally apaurusheya; the 'rishi' field below covers the seer associated with a given mantra, which is a different concept from authorship.

id.notes: e.g. '1.1.1' for Mandala.Sukta.Rik, or 'prapathaka_1.khanda_1' for an Upanishad

reference.notes: human-readable locator, e.g. 'Mandala 1, Sukta 1, Rik 1' or 'Prashna 3, Anuvaka 2'

pada_patha.notes: word-separated form; not always available for every text

svara_notation.notes: accented text with udatta/anudatta/svarita marks, where available

rishi.notes: the seer to whom this mantra is traditionally attributed - distinct from 'authorship'

devata.notes: presiding deity, mainly relevant for Samhita mantras

chandas.notes: metre name, mainly relevant for Samhita mantras

bhashya.notes: [{commentator, text, language}] - e.g. Sayana, Madhva's Rigbhashya, etc. Multiple commentators can be listed

references.notes: [{target, unit_id, note}] -- target is another grantha's slug (e.g. 'puranas/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10'), unit_id is that grantha's own item id being pointed at (e.g. '10.29.1'). Used to build the library-wide backlinks index (see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md) so 'what cites this verse' works without scanning the whole corpus.

tags.notes: free-form keywords for cross-library search -- independent of the taxonomy path itself.

itihasa_purana_text.description: Shared schema for Ramayana, Mahabharata (+ Harivamsha khila), and the 18 Puranas/Upapuranas - all shloka-based Sanskrit narrative organized into sarga/adhyaya/skandha units. A specific Purana can override _schema at its own node in taxonomy.json if it needs extra fields.

author.notes: override this folder's default_author (e.g. Vyasa) if a specific khanda/upapurana has a different traditional attribution

summary.notes: one or two line synopsis of the sarga/adhyaya

shlokas.notes: [{number, sanskrit_text, padaccheda, anvaya, artha, bhashya[]}] - padaccheda/anvaya optional, filled in only where available

references.notes: [{target, unit_id, note}] -- target is another grantha's slug (e.g. 'puranas/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10'), unit_id is that grantha's own item id being pointed at (e.g. '10.29.1'). Used to build the library-wide backlinks index (see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md) so 'what cites this verse' works without scanning the whole corpus.

tags.notes: free-form keywords for cross-library search -- independent of the taxonomy path itself.

smriti_dharmashastra_text.description: The 18 Smritis. Structurally similar to itihasa_purana_text (shloka-based, adhyaya-organized) but with a subject-matter tag since Smritis are organized by legal/ethical topic rather than narrative. Each Smriti's folder carries its own _default_author (its named rishi) in taxonomy.json.

references.notes: [{target, unit_id, note}] -- target is another grantha's slug (e.g. 'puranas/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10'), unit_id is that grantha's own item id being pointed at (e.g. '10.29.1'). Used to build the library-wide backlinks index (see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md) so 'what cites this verse' works without scanning the whole corpus.

tags.notes: free-form keywords for cross-library search -- independent of the taxonomy path itself.

stotra_text.description: Devotional hymns, e.g. Prahlada Krita Narasimha Stotra (DvaitaVedanta/Itara/Stotra/prahlada_kruta_narasimha, folder renamed from pns 23 Aug 2026; internal stotraCode stayed pns for localStorage continuity). Verse-by-verse, with heavier emphasis on audio (these are typically chanted) and a closing phala-shruti (benefits of recitation) section that most stotras have. Each stotra's folder carries its own _default_author in taxonomy.json (e.g. PrahladaKrutaNarasimha -> 'Bhakta Prahlada').

author.notes: who composed this stotra - usually just inherit the folder's default_author; override here only for e.g. an anthology folder mixing several authors' stotras

phala_shruti.notes: benefit-of-recitation text, usually only present on the closing verse(s)

references.notes: [{target, unit_id, note}] -- target is another grantha's slug (e.g. 'puranas/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10'), unit_id is that grantha's own item id being pointed at (e.g. '10.29.1'). Used to build the library-wide backlinks index (see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md) so 'what cites this verse' works without scanning the whole corpus.

tags.notes: free-form keywords for cross-library search -- independent of the taxonomy path itself.

gemini_enrichment.notes: {generated_at, model, segments: [{text, reference_ids?}], references: {ref_id: {...}}} -- written by tools/gemini_enrich.py; segments/references render as footnotes via js/footnote-engine.js. Every reference's 'status' (verified/possible/unresolved) is decided locally by tools/reference_resolution against this corpus, never taken on Gemini's word alone. See PENDING.md, 'Reference Resolution Engine'.

grantha_prakarana_text.description: General-purpose schema for independent Sanskrit prose/shastraic treatises. Used for Vyasakuta granthas (Vyasatirtha, Raghavendra Swami, Vadiraja, etc. - their own independent works, as opposed to Sarvamoola which is Madhva's own corpus and now uses the mula/tika_jayatirtha/tippani split instead - see those three schemas below).

id.notes: e.g. 'sutra_01' or a running paragraph number

author.notes: override the folder's default_author if needed

mula_text.notes: the original Sanskrit text for this unit

tika.notes: [{commentator, text}] - if this particular grantha has its own sub-commentaries

references.notes: [{target, unit_id, note}] -- target is another grantha's slug (e.g. 'puranas/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10'), unit_id is that grantha's own item id being pointed at (e.g. '10.29.1'). Used to build the library-wide backlinks index (see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md) so 'what cites this verse' works without scanning the whole corpus.

tags.notes: free-form keywords for cross-library search -- independent of the taxonomy path itself.

grantha_mula_text.description: The 'mula' (root-text) folder that sits inside every Sarvamoola work (e.g. sarvamoola_grantha/gita_prasthana/gita_bhashya/mula). Holds Sri Madhvacharya's own original Sanskrit text, unit by unit.

id.notes: e.g. 'sutra_01', or a paragraph/verse number as appropriate to this particular work

sanskrit_text.notes: Madhvacharya's original text for this unit

artha.notes: plain-language paraphrase, if you want one independent of any tika

references.notes: [{target, unit_id, note}] -- target is another grantha's slug (e.g. 'puranas/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10'), unit_id is that grantha's own item id being pointed at (e.g. '10.29.1'). Used to build the library-wide backlinks index (see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md) so 'what cites this verse' works without scanning the whole corpus.

grantha_tika_text.description: The 'tika_jayatirtha' folder that sits inside every Sarvamoola work. Holds Sri Jayatirtha's commentary specifically (each of his tikas on different Sarvamoola works has its own traditional title - e.g. Nyayasudha, Tattvaprakashika, Prameyadipika - store that title per-item rather than in the folder name, since one folder covers one tika text throughout).

id.notes: matches the corresponding 'mula' item's id where possible, for cross-reference

tika_title.notes: the traditional name of Jayatirtha's commentary on this specific work, e.g. 'Nyayasudha', 'Tattvaprakashika'

sanskrit_text.notes: Jayatirtha's commentary text for this unit

references.notes: [{target, unit_id, note}] -- target is another grantha's slug (e.g. 'puranas/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10'), unit_id is that grantha's own item id being pointed at (e.g. '10.29.1'). Used to build the library-wide backlinks index (see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md) so 'what cites this verse' works without scanning the whole corpus.

grantha_tippani_text.description: The 'tippani' folder that sits inside every Sarvamoola work. Holds independent sub-commentaries by later acharyas (Raghavendra Swami, Vadiraja, Vyasatirtha, Satyanatha Tirtha, etc.) on that specific work or on Jayatirtha's tika. See tippanikaras.json for the registry of known Tippanikara authors this field's 'author' should reference.

author.notes: the Tippanikara's name - should match an entry in tippanikaras.json

tippani_title.notes: the traditional name of this specific tippani, if it has one

references.notes: [{target, unit_id, note}] -- target is another grantha's slug (e.g. 'puranas/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10'), unit_id is that grantha's own item id being pointed at (e.g. '10.29.1'). dasa_sahitya_composition.description: Kannada devotional compositions by the Haridasas (Dasakuta). Each Dasa's folder carries its own _default_author in taxonomy.json, with sub-folders by composition type (pada_kirtane, suladi, ugabhoga, mundige, dandaka, other_compositions).

ankita_nama.notes: the composer's signature/pen-name embedded in the composition, e.g. 'Purandara Vittala', 'Vijaya Vittala'

raga_tala.notes: musical setting, where relevant (especially for pada/kirtane and suladi)

references.notes: [{target, unit_id, note}] -- target is another grantha's slug (e.g. 'puranas/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10'), unit_id is that grantha's own item id being pointed at (e.g. '10.29.1'). Used to build the library-wide backlinks index (see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md) so 'what cites this verse' works without scanning the whole corpus.

tags.notes: free-form keywords for cross-library search -- independent of the taxonomy path itself.

dasa_pada_text.description: A single Haridasa devotional composition (pada/suladi/ugabhoga/...) imported from the public Haridasa-sahitya web archives via tools/DvaitaVedanta/Itara/DasaSahitya/. Kannada is the primary text; IAST/Devanagari are auto-transliterated.

form.notes: pada | suladi | ugabhoga | devaranama | aarati | mangala | kolu | shobhane | laali | dashavatara | sampradaya | kavya | mundige | dandaka | other

title.notes: {kn, latin, iast, devanagari} -- kn is the source title, the rest are auto-transliterated (or source-supplied romanization for 'latin')

text.notes: {kannada, iast, devanagari, source_roman} -- each a string[][] of stanzas -> lines; kannada is primary, the rest auto-transliterated (source_roman only when the source page supplied its own romanization)

meaning.notes: word-meaning/artha block, when the source page has one

source.notes: {site, url, attribution, fetched} -- every record keeps a visible source URL, non-commercial dharma-prachara/education/research use

also_at.notes: other source URLs this same composition (by dedup fingerprint) was also found at
